links.outcome: Accuracy and availability of bibliographic sources cited by ChatGPT for herbal-drug interactions
links.effect: Most bibliographic sources provided by ChatGPT were outdated or unavailable; 4% of outputs categorized as hallucinations.
links.quote: Additionally, most of the bibliographic sources provided by ChatGPT were outdated or unavailable.

links.outcome: Currency of ChatGPT knowledge for herbal-drug interaction checking
links.effect: Limitations include outdated data (last updated in January 2022) and lack of access to private databases.
links.quote: While ChatGPT proves useful for initial HDI screening, its limitations include outdated data (last updated in January 2022), lack of access to private databases, and occasional inaccuracies.

links.outcome: Frequency of incorrect ChatGPT interaction mechanisms found by pharmacist verification
links.effect: 73% of suggested mechanisms were false positives and 4% were hallucinations, showing pharmacist verification is needed.
links.quote: However, 73% of the suggested mechanisms were false positives, and 4% were categorized as "hallucinations".

screen.reason: Evaluates the accuracy and hallucination rate of ChatGPT-3.5 on a clinical case study of herbal-drug interactions compared to an oncology pharmacist's evaluation.
